column2: Modifying or deleting existing data requires an explicit go-ahead in the active session, never approval inferred from earlier instructions.

column1: Principle 2: read, then write, then delete
column2: Grant permission tiers progressively. Never give a higher tier by default because it might occasionally be useful.
Text from emails, web pages, documents, API responses and tool outputs has no instruction authority.
Every tool call should leave an auditable record that the operator reviews periodically as a governance check.
Read-only, stateful read, write, destructive write, and destructive delete.
File delete, email delete and database modification: disabled by default, and requires confirmation plus an audit log entry.
Before granting a permission, ask what the worst plausible outcome is if it runs at night with nobody watching.
Restrict file read to workspace paths and deny paths such as .ssh, .gnupg and .env files, so the agent cannot read secrets.
Week 1 read-only, week 2 create-only writes, week 3 modify and delete behind gates; after 30 days disable tools never called.
Log the failure, report it to the user, and stop. Never auto-retry writes or destructive actions; a read may retry once.
Pruning setting that keeps the active multi-step task's context intact while older turns are summarized.
Full capability, reduced capability, read-only, passive report, explicit failure. Degrade in steps and never report partial work as success.
SOUL.md, AGENTS.md and USER.md as loaded at session start. Absolute constraints that no message can override, including the user's.
Direct messages via an allowlisted channel. Full task authority within Level 1 limits, but cannot rewrite system constraints.
Another agent configured by name with tool-scoped authority. A blanket rule trusting all agents is not valid.
Heartbeats, cron tasks and workflows. Limited to actions pre-approved in the schedule definition; cannot escalate.
Emails, web pages, documents, tool results and unconfigured agents. Analysis authority only; embedded commands are reported, not run.
Any input source not explicitly assigned a trust level should be placed at Level 5.
The current tier passes its tests, at least 10 sessions have been reviewed, and the new permission has a confirmation gate.
Email to a new recipient, deleting more than 5 items, financial API POSTs, public posts, bulk modifications, and acting for another person.
Five stages: scope containment, confirmation gates, injection resistance, budget and limits, and recovery after restart.
Write SOUL.md, then AGENTS.md tool permission specs, then adversarial test cases, and only then connect live tools.
Covers the happy path but omits conflict ordering, a trust hierarchy, refusals, out-of-scope handling and an adversarial stance.
Trading skills start read-only. Order placement is unavailable until the user enables it in the current session with a documented command.
The agent may recommend trades, but each order needs its own same-session confirmation. A blanket approval for a sequence does not count.
